author: Temminck & Schlegel, 1844
summary: 우리나라에 드물게 찾아오는 겨울철새로, 농경지와 평지, 간척지, 트인 땅에서 지낸다. 부드러운 날갯짓으로 날며 쥐와 곤충, 작은 새 등을 잡아먹는다. 세계 개체 수에 관한 구체적인 자료는 없으나, 주식인 설치류의 수와 개체 수가 관계있을 것으로 본다. 티베트, 러시아, 몽골 등지에서 번식한다.

art.subject: Upland Buzzard (Buteo hemilasius), adult pale morph, as seen over Korean farmland in winter: head whitish-buff with fine dark streaks; upperparts and upperwing coverts pale sandy-brown with darker feather centres; a large whitish patch at the base of the primaries on the upperwing; breast whitish-buff lightly streaked; belly and thighs dark brown, forming a dark lower belly and dark 'trousers'; underwing whitish with large blackish carpal patches and black wingtips; tail pale greyish-white, finely barred grey. Short hooked dark bill with a yellow cere; legs feathered on the front for more than half their length; bare toes yellow.
art.pose: flying low over open fields with supple wingbeats, searching for prey
art.scene: Korean winter open farmland and flat reclaimed land under a wide sky; no people, buildings or text
art.build: The largest buzzard in Korea, clearly bigger and longer-winged than Eastern Buzzard, approaching a small eagle in bulk. Heavy body, rounded head, short hooked bill. Long, broad wings with well-fingered tips. Tail medium length, fan-shaped when spread. Soars and glides on wings raised in a shallow V, often hovers over fields, and flies with slow, supple, elastic wingbeats.
avoid: Do not paint a white tail with a broad dark terminal band — that is Rough-legged Buzzard (Buteo lagopus).
Do not paint a dark brown head and an evenly barred brown tail like Eastern Buzzard (Buteo japonicus).
Do not paint fully bare legs; the front of the tarsus is feathered.
Do not paint an eagle with a long heavy bill or a long wedge-shaped tail.
